## reference · AI platform citation source index 2026

- **Data Scope**: The 2026 Index synthesizes >680 million citations across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, Gemini, and Claude, derived from six major studies conducted between August 2024 and April 2026.
- **Top Source**: Reddit is the #1 cited source across all major AI engines, capturing ~40% of all citations.
- **Concentration**: The top 15 domains absorb 68% of the total AI citation share, indicating higher concentration than historical Google PageRank.
- **Platform-Specific Leaders**:
  - **ChatGPT**: Heavily relies on Wikipedia (26–48% of top-10 citation share), Reddit, Forbes, and Business Insider.
  - **Perplexity**: Prioritizes primary sources, NIH/PubMed, and named B2B authority.
  - **Claude**: Leans toward high-quality journalism (NYT, The Atlantic, The New Yorker, The Economist).
  - **Google AI Overviews**: Dominated by YouTube, which holds a 200x citation advantage over other video sources.
- **Volatility**: Citation share shifts within weeks, not years. Example: ChatGPT’s Reddit citation share dropped from ~60% to 10% in six weeks (late 2025) following a Google parameter change; displaced share was absorbed by PR Newswire, Forbes, and Medium.
- **Content Type Impact**:
  - Journalism accounts for 27% of all AI citations but rises to 49% for time-sensitive queries.
  - User-generated content (UGC) structurally outweighs journalism for non-time-sensitive queries.
  - Claude cites journalism from the past 12 months at a 36% rate, compared to 56% for ChatGPT.
- **Strategic Priorities**:
  - Audit brand presence across the top 15 sources before addressing the long tail.
  - Treat Wikipedia as foundational infrastructure.
  - Build Reddit as a strategic, evergreen channel.
  - Map journalism targets to specific platform citation patterns.
  - Plan for volatility as a baseline condition, not a tail risk.
- **Categorization**: The 50 sources are grouped into six buckets: Community & Conversation, Encyclopedic & Reference, Professional & Identity, Video & Audio, Editorial & News, and Commerce & Review.
